title: 3,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene and HCl
subtitle: A methyl shift before chloride adds

reactants.caption: 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene + hydrogen chloride
reactants.learnerPrompt: The alkene reacts with HCl. Draw the protonation.
hintTiers: The π bond takes the proton. Which end gives the more stable cation?
The H goes on the CH₂ end, so the cation is secondary. The H–Cl bond breaks onto chlorine. Two arrows.
Arrow 1: from the C=C π bond to the H, forming a bond from the CH₂ carbon to H. Arrow 2: from the H–Cl bond onto chlorine.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That leaves a primary cation on the CH₂ carbon. Put the H on the CH₂ carbon instead.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right start. Hydrogen can only have one bond: break the H–Cl bond onto chlorine.

secondary-cation.caption: a secondary cation next to a tert-butyl group
secondary-cation.learnerPrompt: This cation can become more stable before chloride arrives. Draw the rearrangement.
hintTiers: The neighbouring carbon has three methyl groups. Can one of them move?
A methyl group moves, with the two electrons of its bond, from the quaternary carbon to the cationic carbon. One arrow.
From the bond between the quaternary carbon and one methyl to a new bond between that methyl and the positively charged carbon. The charge moves to the quaternary carbon, which becomes tertiary.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That only takes the proton back: the reverse of the last step.

tertiary-cation.caption: the rearranged tertiary cation
hintTiers: Where is the positive charge now?
Chloride gives a lone pair to the tertiary cationic carbon. One arrow.
From a chloride lone pair to the positively charged carbon, forming the C–Cl bond.

steps.explanationAfterStep: A secondary cation forms, next to a carbon carrying three methyl groups.
A 1,2-methyl shift: the methyl keeps its bonding pair, so the positive charge moves to the carbon it left. Secondary becomes tertiary.
Chloride traps the tertiary cation. The carbon skeleton has changed: the main product is not the simple Markovnikov product.
Also correct, but minor: chloride catches some secondary cation before the methyl shift.

mechanismSummary: Protonation gives a secondary cation next to a quaternary carbon. A methyl group moves with its bonding pair to the cationic carbon (a 1,2-methyl shift), giving a more stable tertiary cation. Chloride adds there: 2-chloro-2,3-dimethylbutane is the main product. Some chloride traps the secondary cation first, giving 3-chloro-2,2-dimethylbutane.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 20
